name: Fertiliser supply
summary: Egyptian urea near $535 a tonne after gas cuts; Gulf nitrogen exports still depend on an impeded Strait of Hormuz
state: Egyptian granular urea fetched about $535 a tonne FOB in November contracts, up about 17% from September, after gas supplies to fertiliser plants were rationed from 1 Nov; producers say export commitments are still being met (Fertilizer Daily, 9 Nov). Gulf exports rely on the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran ordered a tighter closure on 23 Nov (Euronews). No export bans by several major exporters were found as of 25 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Farmers buying nitrogen fertiliser for spring face higher prices than before the Gulf conflict. Food producers may see input costs feed into crop prices later.
rubric_hit: Watch: key Gulf export route impeded via Hormuz; no multi-exporter bans or >60% 3-month urea rise for Alert

sources.title: Fertilizer Daily — Egyptian urea price rises amid gas cuts
Euronews — Iran orders Hormuz closed 'further day by day' as Qatar seeks to revive peace talks

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
